literature_notes: Three ledger lines cover NCAM2 but none grounds an extracellular surface tag site. L1 reports an HA-tagged full-length transmembrane NCAM2 construct, but the ΔED logic (the same HA tag is retained in NCAM2ΔED comprising only aa 694–837) eliminates placement at the extracellular N-terminus (residues 20–693 are deleted in ΔED). The tag therefore lies within aa 694–837, but no residue or loop is named, and the position is ambiguous between the 11-residue juxtamembrane ectodomain stub (694–704) and the intracellular tail (726–837). Topology_derived requires exactly one unambiguous extracellular terminus; the ΔED evidence removes that certainty here. Doubt → site dropped. L2 and L3 both describe a C-terminally Myc-DDK-tagged transmembrane mouse NCAM2; the C-terminus (residue 837) is intracellular per the topology landmarks (intracellular: 726–837), so this tag is not a surface site and is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Myc-DDK tag on transmembrane mouse NCAM2 used in HEK-cell BACE1 cleavage assay; residue 837 is intracellular per topology landmarks (intracellular: 726–837).
Same C-terminally Myc-DDK-tagged NCAM2-TM construct transfected into HEK cells to study BACE1-mediated proteolytic processing; C-terminus is intracellular.
